bull_bear.body:
- ~INR230 cr cash/treasury; generating ~INR40 cr+ FCF/yr → recurring "cash pile" problem.
- M&A budget ~INR140 cr flagged earlier; 3-4 consultants engaged (France, UK, US); "few advanced discussions," expect "something by year-end" (Q1/Q2 unlikely). Target by year-end FY27.

- Treasury mix: ~5-7% equity MF; ~30-35% FDs; ~30-35% treasury bonds; rest AAA corporate bonds (e.g., Tata Capital). Liquidatable within 3-4 days; FDs/bonds laddered to mature.

bull_bear.title: Non-obvious Insights

bull_bear.body:
- M&A is one of four stated strategic priorities; the company is "actively looking for M&A opportunities across globe preferably in the EU and the USA", targeting manufacturers or distributors in molecular, microbiology, immunology and similar IVD segments.
- Acquisition discipline is explicit: over the last 2 years several IVD companies were evaluated but valuations were high on the back of Covid profits and "the Sales & EBITDA were not matching our IRR or future growth possibility, hence we did not proceed".
- Funds will also be deployed into the joint venture created in Manchester, UK "depending on the need"; the Coris deal is framed as strengthening credibility "as a genuine buyer".
- Working capital is being run loose by design - a liberal credit policy to avoid losing customers to post-COVID competition results in "higher debtor level currently which we will gradually bring down in the coming years" - while the agro business "operates with minimal debt".

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Price and margin pressure from increasing competition, particularly lower-priced products — The report states that increasing competition, particularly from lower-priced products, continued to put pressure on pricing and margins in the international business; for Coris, segments other than AMR may face some pressure from Chinese competition in FY 2026-27.
- Regulatory registration timelines gate commercial entry into new international markets — Regulatory registrations remain an important part of the international expansion strategy, and depending on the country and regulatory pathway, registrations can take approximately 10-15 months from initiation before commercial business can commence, delaying revenue conversion.
- EU IVDR transition dependency for the key TRUPCR Class C portfolio — Continued access to the European market depends on completing technical documentation evaluations and obtaining IVDR certification; eligible legacy Class C IVDs may continue on the EU market only until 31st December 2028 subject to fulfilment of prescribed conditions, with Notified Body application and written agreement deadlines of 26th May 2026 and 26th September 2026.
- Geopolitical tensions and global trade/logistics disruption — The report says geopolitical tensions and disruptions in global trade and logistics affected business conversion and movement of goods in certain regions, and also contributed to supply-chain disruption affecting the agrochemicals division.
- Export and international concentration of the diagnostics business — TRUPCR products reach more than 70 countries and over 200 customers, with the Middle East and Europe described as important contributors and growth dependent on new market entries, international tenders and distributor networks, so performance is exposed to external market and tender outcomes.
- Agrochemicals division exposure to agricultural demand variability and monsoon conditions — The decline in that division's sales was attributed mainly to variability in demand from the agricultural sector, with uneven and prolonged monsoon conditions in the Kharif season affecting the timing of crop protection applications and demand for agrochemical products.
- Uncertain commercialisation of newer technology verticals (NGS and digital PCR) — Management states TRUNGS traction from customers is very low, the NGS market is at a nascent stage and highly competitive with labs making their own homebrew kits, benefits are difficult to quantify or forecast, and dPCR products launched in Q3 FY 2025-26 are at a very initial stage with nominal sales.
- Integration and earn-out execution risk on the Coris BioConcept acquisition — The acquisition (70% by 3B along with its UK subsidiary TPE) carried an upfront cash consideration of GBP 2.15 million plus an earn-out, completed on 29th August 2025, and under Ind AS consolidation runs only from the acquisition date, so reported results and the expected benefits depend on the acquired business performing as expected.

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Expansion for 3B BlackBio Dx is geographic, regulatory and acquisition-led rather than plant-led; the annual report describes no new manufacturing plant, line or capacity addition. The TRUPCR(r) portfolio reached more than 70 countries and over 200 customers across Europe, the Middle East, Asia-Pacific, Latin America, Africa and North America, with new markets added across APAC and Africa during FY 2025-26 following completion of product registrations and tendering processes, and a recent entry into the Southeast Asian market. Management notes that regulatory registrations are an integral part of the international expansion strategy and that, depending on country and pathway, a registration can take approximately 10-15 months from initiation before commercial business can commence. On the regulatory front, the Company is transitioning its key TRUPCR(r) portfolio to EU IVDR (Regulation (EU) 2017/746): BSI Group has been appointed Notified Body with the required agreement in place, the IVDR-aligned Quality Management System audits by BSI were completed in November 2025, and technical document review for the identified product groups is ongoing, with the Company targeting IVDR certification of its key Class C TRUPCR(r) products ahead of the transitional deadlines (IVDR-compliant QMS by 26 May 2025, application to a Notified Body by 26 May 2026, written agreement with the Notified Body by 26 September 2026, with eligible legacy Class C IVDs placeable on the EU market until 31 December 2028). The principal inorganic step was the acquisition of Coris BioConcept SRL, Belgium (a 30-year-old manufacturer of rapid diagnostic solutions): 3B BlackBio Dx (70%) together with its UK subsidiary acquired the business for an upfront cash consideration of GBP 2.15 million including net cash and customary working capital adjustments, with an earn-out component referenced at GBP 2.765 million; completion took place on 29 August 2025 and consolidation runs from the acquisition date. Coris Holding SRL, Belgium is a direct subsidiary (70%) acquired 29 August 2025 and itself owns 100% of Coris BioConcept SRL. Coris has initiated US FDA registration for RESIST-5, which is expected to open opportunities in the US and other markets recognising FDA approvals from FY 2027-28 onwards, and IVDR certification for two of its key AMR products is expected to support further market growth. In the UK, subsidiary TRUPCR(r) Europe Limited (70%, acquired 28 March 2022) is expanding its footprint from its Manchester facility, which provides faster deliveries, local technical support and closer customer engagement, and is gradually extending its reach beyond Europe into Latin America, Africa and other geographies; the Company states it will also deploy some funds in the joint venture created in Manchester, UK depending on the need. The Company is actively looking for further M&A opportunities globally, preferably in the EU and the USA, for manufacturers or distributors in the IVD segment spanning molecular, microbiology, immunology and similar areas; an earlier candidate was not pursued because its sales and EBITDA did not match the Company's IRR or future growth expectations. Product-platform build-out continues through R&D rather than capacity: the TRURAPID(r) AMR range (RESIST-5 OKNVI, RESIST ACINETO, RESIST CTX-M) is to be progressively expanded as new products complete development and regulatory requirements; digital PCR (dPCR) assays were commercially launched in Q3 FY 2025-26 though sales remain nominal; and TRUNGS(r) NGS products BRCA Plus Kit and MTB-MDR NGS Kit are to be launched commercially after extensive R&D, with management cautioning that NGS is nascent, highly competitive and unlikely to deliver major growth immediately. In the agrochemicals division the focus is on government and institutional procurement through GeM and other tendering platforms and on brand visibility in micro-fertilizers, bio-fertilizers and public health products; the division remains debt-free. On the energy side, installation and commissioning of a 40KW solar power plant was finished in August 2022, and energy-conservation measures include conversion of all light fittings to LED.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- The Indian molecular diagnostics market continued to grow during FY2025-26, supported by the increasing need for early, accurate and reliable diagnosis of infectious diseases, cancer and genetic disorders.
- Adoption of molecular technologies such as real-time PCR, next-generation sequencing and digital PCR is increasing across hospitals, diagnostic laboratories and specialised testing centers, improving both the scope and accessibility of molecular testing; the growing focus on genomics and precision medicine is also contributing to sector development.
- Government initiatives under Ayushman Bharat, the National Health Mission and disease-specific programmes such as the National TB Elimination Programme are supporting wider access to diagnostic services, including molecular testing.
- Expansion of molecular diagnostic testing and strengthening of diagnostic facilities at regional and sub-district levels are driving adoption beyond major urban centers.
- The Government's focus on domestic manufacturing and self-reliance in healthcare has encouraged development and production of diagnostic products within India; increasing domestic capabilities in assay development, molecular testing and genomics, with continued private-sector investment, are improving availability of advanced and cost-effective diagnostic solutions.
- Management states the molecular diagnostics sector in India is expected to maintain a positive growth trajectory over the coming years, driven by greater awareness of early diagnosis, increasing adoption of precision medicine, expansion of healthcare infrastructure and continued development of indigenous diagnostic technologies.
- Export growth momentum was supported by increasing business from existing markets, expansion of the distribution network, new product registrations, participation in international tenders and successful product validations with key customers; new markets were added across APAC and Africa after completion of product registrations and tendering processes.
- The Middle East and Europe remain important contributors to international business, while efforts to build a stronger presence across Southeast Asia, Africa and Latin America are progressing steadily.
- Margin/pricing pressure: increasing competition, particularly from lower-priced products, continued to put pressure on pricing and margins; geopolitical tensions and disruptions in global trade and logistics affected business conversion and movement of goods in certain regions.
- Differentiation levers cited: quality and reliability of products, a wide molecular diagnostics portfolio, established distributor and customer relationships, ability to respond quickly to customer requirements, and faster order fulfilment (particularly for European customers) with responsive technical and application support.
- Management says it expects the export business to maintain a positive growth trajectory in FY2026-27, supported by new market entries, a growing customer base and continued demand for molecular diagnostic solutions.
- Agrochemicals: the sales decline was mainly due to variability in demand from the agricultural sector, with an uneven and prolonged monsoon in the Kharif season affecting the timing of crop protection applications and agrochemical demand, compounded by geopolitical tensions and supply-chain disruptions; despite this the division improved operating performance and returned to profitability and remains debt-free.
- NGS: management states the NGS market is at a very nascent stage and dominated by whole genome sequencing, whole exome sequencing and NIPT; TRUNGS traction is very low, commercialization is challenging because the field is highly competitive and labs make their own homebrew kits, so management does not expect major high growth or revenue from NGS immediately, only gradual growth.
- Coris: management says it expects Coris to be EBITDA positive in the next financial year, with the AMR portfolio expected to grow while other product segments may face pressure from Chinese competition; IVDR certification for two key AMR products is expected to support further market growth and US FDA registration of RESIST-5 is expected to open US and FDA-recognising markets from FY2027-28.

Coris Holding SRL, Belgium is a direct subsidiary (70%) acquired 29 August 2025 and itself owns 100% of Coris BioConcept SRL. In the agrochemicals division the focus is on government and institutional procurement through GeM and other tendering platforms and on brand visibility in micro-fertilizers, bio-fertilizers and public health products; the division remains debt-free. demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- The Indian molecular diagnostics market continued to grow during FY2025-26, supported by the increasing need for early, accurate and reliable diagnosis of infectious diseases, cancer and genetic disorders.
- Adoption of molecular technologies such as real-time PCR, next-generation sequencing and digital PCR is increasing across hospitals, diagnostic laboratories and specialised testing centers, improving both the scope and accessibility of molecular testing; the growing focus on genomics and precision medicine is also contributing to sector development.
- Government initiatives under Ayushman Bharat, the National Health Mission and disease-specific programmes such as the National TB Elimination Programme are supporting wider access to diagnostic services, including molecular testing.
- Expansion of molecular diagnostic testing and strengthening of diagnostic facilities at regional and sub-district levels are driving adoption beyond major urban centers.
- The Government's focus on domestic manufacturing and self-reliance in healthcare has encouraged development and production of diagnostic products within India; increasing domestic capabilities in assay development, molecular testing and genomics, with continued private-sector investment, are improving availability of advanced and cost-effective diagnostic solutions.
- Management states the molecular diagnostics sector in India is expected to maintain a positive growth trajectory over the coming years, driven by greater awareness of early diagnosis, increasing adoption of precision medicine, expansion of healthcare infrastructure and continued development of indigenous diagnostic technologies.
- Export growth momentum was supported by increasing business from existing markets, expansion of the distribution network, new product registrations, participation in international tenders and successful product validations with key customers; new markets were added across APAC and Africa after completion of product registrations and tendering processes.
- The Middle East and Europe remain important contributors to international business, while efforts to build a stronger presence across Southeast Asia, Africa and Latin America are progressing steadily.
- Margin/pricing pressure: increasing competition, particularly from lower-priced products, continued to put pressure on pricing and margins; geopolitical tensions and disruptions in global trade and logistics affected business conversion and movement of goods in certain regions.
- Differentiation levers cited: quality and reliability of products, a wide molecular diagnostics portfolio, established distributor and customer relationships, ability to respond quickly to customer requirements, and faster order fulfilment (particularly for European customers) with responsive technical and application support.
- Management says it expects the export business to maintain a positive growth trajectory in FY2026-27, supported by new market entries, a growing customer base and continued demand for molecular diagnostic solutions.
- Agrochemicals: the sales decline was mainly due to variability in demand from the agricultural sector, with an uneven and prolonged monsoon in the Kharif season affecting the timing of crop protection applications and agrochemical demand, compounded by geopolitical tensions and supply-chain disruptions; despite this the division improved operating performance and returned to profitability and remains debt-free.
- NGS: management states the NGS market is at a very nascent stage and dominated by whole genome sequencing, whole exome sequencing and NIPT; TRUNGS traction is very low, commercialization is challenging because the field is highly competitive and labs make their own homebrew kits, so management does not expect major high growth or revenue from NGS immediately, only gradual growth.
- Coris: management says it expects Coris to be EBITDA positive in the next financial year, with the AMR portfolio expected to grow while other product segments may face pressure from Chinese competition; IVDR certification for two key AMR products is expected to support further market growth and US FDA registration of RESIST-5 is expected to open US and FDA-recognising markets from FY2027-28.
- Management states that availability of facilities with the right blend of technology, a vast distribution network, adequate financial resources, a stable tax regime and motivated manpower will facilitate continued growth across businesses and product categories in domestic and international markets.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Expansion for 3B BlackBio Dx is geographic, regulatory and acquisition-led rather than plant-led; the annual report describes no new manufacturing plant, line or capacity addition. The TRUPCR(r) portfolio reached more than 70 countries and over 200 customers across Europe, the Middle East, Asia-Pacific, Latin America, Africa and North America, with new markets added across APAC and Africa during FY 2025-26 following completion of product registrations and tendering processes, and a recent entry into the Southeast Asian market. Management notes that regulatory registrations are an integral part of the international expansion strategy and that, depending on country and pathway, a registration can take approximately 10-15 months from initiation before commercial business can commence. On the regulatory front, the Company is transitioning its key TRUPCR(r) portfolio to EU IVDR (Regulation (EU) 2017/746): BSI Group has been appointed Notified Body with the required agreement in place, the IVDR-aligned Quality Management System audits by BSI were completed in November 2025, and technical document review for the identified product groups is ongoing, with the Company targeting IVDR certification of its key Class C TRUPCR(r) products ahead of the transitional deadlines (IVDR-compliant QMS by 26 May 2025, application to a Notified Body by 26 May 2026, written agreement with the Notified Body by 26 September 2026, with eligible legacy Class C IVDs placeable on the EU market until 31 December 2028). The principal inorganic step was the acquisition of Coris BioConcept SRL, Belgium (a 30-year-old manufacturer of rapid diagnostic solutions): 3B BlackBio Dx (70%) together with its UK subsidiary acquired the business for an upfront cash consideration of GBP 2.15 million including net cash and customary working capital adjustments, with an earn-out component referenced at GBP 2.765 million; completion took place on 29 August 2025 and consolidation runs from the acquisition date. Coris Holding SRL, Belgium is a direct subsidiary (70%) acquired 29 August 2025 and itself owns 100% of Coris BioConcept SRL. Coris has initiated US FDA registration for RESIST-5, which is expected to open opportunities in the US and other markets recognising FDA approvals from FY 2027-28 onwards, and IVDR certification for two of its key AMR products is expected to support further market growth. In the UK, subsidiary TRUPCR(r) Europe Limited (70%, acquired 28 March 2022) is expanding its footprint from its Manchester facility, which provides faster deliveries, local technical support and closer customer engagement, and is gradually extending its reach beyond Europe into Latin America, Africa and other geographies; the Company states it will also deploy some funds in the joint venture created in Manchester, UK depending on the need. The Company is actively looking for further M&A opportunities globally, preferably in the EU and the USA, for manufacturers or distributors in the IVD segment spanning molecular, microbiology, immunology and similar areas; an earlier candidate was not pursued because its sales and EBITDA did not match the Company's IRR or future growth expectations. Product-platform build-out continues through R&D rather than capacity: the TRURAPID(r) AMR range (RESIST-5 OKNVI, RESIST ACINETO, RESIST CTX-M) is to be progressively expanded as new products complete development and regulatory requirements; digital PCR (dPCR) assays were commercially launched in Q3 FY 2025-26 though sales remain nominal; and TRUNGS(r) NGS products BRCA Plus Kit and MTB-MDR NGS Kit are to be launched commercially after extensive R&D, with management cautioning that NGS is nascent, highly competitive and unlikely to deliver major growth immediately. In the agrochemicals division the focus is on government and institutional procurement through GeM and other tendering platforms and on brand visibility in micro-fertilizers, bio-fertilizers and public health products; the division remains debt-free. On the energy side, installation and commissioning of a 40KW solar power plant was finished in August 2022, and energy-conservation measures include conversion of all light fittings to LED.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Wide molecular diagnostics portfolio spanning PCR, NGS, digital PCR and rapid lateral-flow tests, allowing the company to offer molecular diagnostics solutions to customers under one roof
- Established international reach — TRUPCR® products reaching more than 70 countries and over 200 customers across Europe, the Middle East, Asia-Pacific, Latin America, Africa and North America
- Ability to respond quickly to customer requirements, with faster order fulfilment (particularly for European customers) and responsive technical and application support differentiating the products
- Local European presence through TRUPCR® Europe Limited's Manchester facility enabling faster deliveries and local technical support
- Regulatory capability: progress toward IVDR certification with BSI as Notified Body and country registrations (which take about 10-15 months) acting as an entry barrier in export markets
- R&D-led new product development — PCR, extraction kits, NGS and digital PCR assays developed in-house, with R&D spend at 3.51% of total turnover
- Coris BioConcept's rapid lateral-flow AMR portfolio complements the molecular range, including an LFT for sleeping sickness described as holding a global monopoly
- Agrochemicals business is debt-free and maintains overall sales stability

risks.title: Risks
risks.body:
- Domestic growth slowed to ~2-3% YoY last two quarters (post high FY24/25 base + FY25 flu/dengue exceptional INR4.2 cr).
- Chinese low-cost competition in high-volume respiratory/Entero rapid tests (hits ~23% of Coris non-AMR mix).
- Middle East geopolitical tension hit some export markets in FY26.
- US FDA timeline uncertainty (could slip beyond 1.5 yrs).
- HAT order is lumpy, Congo-specific, Ebola-exposed; one-time PAT contributor that fades.
- Coris H1 FY27 EBITDA losses; consolidation of unprofitable quarters drags reported H1.
- M&A execution risk — valuation gap (sellers at 20x).

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious Insights
non_obvious.body:
- The INR60 cr consolidated PAT is flattered by Coris's HAT order landing in the consolidated (profitable) 7-month window — sustainable Coris is barely EBITDA-positive.
- "Only two earnings calls/year" going forward reduces disclosure cadence — watch for less granularity.
- Renaming Kilpest → 3B BlackBio Dx completes identity shift to pure diagnostics.
- Real moat = IVDR + (pending) US FDA as regulatory barriers that keep Chinese volume players out of AMR/oncology/high-panel niches.
- Pricing chain: kit sold to distributor ~INR700-800 → hospital buys ~INR1,000 → end test billed ~INR2,000-2,500.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Expand the TRUPCR molecular diagnostics footprint internationally — deepen penetration in existing markets, convert ongoing regulatory registrations into commercial business, enter newer territories, and strengthen the distributor and institutional customer network.
- Pursue international tenders and register a wider range of products in key markets as a core part of the international expansion strategy (registrations take approximately 10-15 months depending on country and regulatory pathway).
- Complete the transition of the key TRUPCR product portfolio to EU IVDR (Regulation (EU) 2017/746) …

challenges.title: Challenges → Beneficiaries
challenges.body:
- *Challenge:* Chinese low-cost respiratory/rapid-test glut pressures commodity assays → *beneficiary tilt:* AMR/oncology/high-panel niche players (3B/Coris) with regulatory moats (IVDR/FDA). ✅ self-beneficiary via menu mix-shift to AMR.
- *Challenge:* US AMR market import-dependent, FDA-gated → ⭐ optionality beneficiary = Coris Resist-5 on clearance (INR100 cr market, currently served by a French exporter via FDA-registered US distributor).
- Beneficiaries (external listed names): none clearly identified.

qoq_log.title: QoQ Log
qoq_log.body:
- **Q4 FY26 (this call):** First call reflecting FULL consolidation of Coris (7 mo) + TRUPCR + 3B. Consol rev ~INR142 cr, PAT ~INR60 cr. Guidance FY27: 15-20% rev & EBITDA growth; topline build to ~INR175-180 cr. Coris EBITDA-flat FY27, 10% by FY28-29. US FDA (Resist-5) targeted FY28. IVDR QMS audits done (BSI). Sample-to-answer OEM installs from Q3 FY27. ~INR230 cr treasury, M&A "by year-end." Cadence cut to 2 calls/yr.
- *(Prior quarters referenced by mgmt: sample-to-answer & POC mentioned last call; M&A candidates met in Dubai; competition commentary unchanged QoQ. No structured prior note on file.)*

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Acquisition] Coris BioConcept SRL, Belgium was acquired on 29th August 2025; under Ind AS consolidation runs only from the acquisition date, so this is the first year Q1 numbers are consolidated versus a non-consolidated prior year.
- [Contract] Coris holds a Belgium Government HAT order (test for the parasite causing African sleeping sickness) of EUR 6.0M received in February 2024 to be supplied over 4 years; a EUR 1.41M HAT order was recently confirmed for supply in Q3 (December 2026) versus EUR 1.35M supplied in December 2025. Coris earnings are seasonal - Q1 and Q2 loss-making, Q3 and Q4 profitable on HAT supply.
- [Regulation] EU IVDR (Regulation 2017/746) applies from 26 May 2026; the company can continue selling as legacy devices until 31 December 2028 (transition period), by which time IVDR certifications are expected.
- [Segment mix / risk] Within Coris, AMR grew 12% and is 70% of sales, while the remaining 30% de-grew 54% "because of Chinese competition"; geopolitical tensions are repeatedly cited as delaying or cancelling export orders and complicating logistics.
- [Legacy division] The agrochemicals division is run for stability, not growth - focused on GeM electronic government tenders for vector-borne disease control, exports mainly to Bangladesh, and supply to old customers - with an existing catalogue spanning chemicals (insecticides 70, fungicides 15, herbicides 11, public health 11) and biologicals (bio pesticide 07, health & hygiene 06, bio fertilizers 05).

US could become ~20% of Coris revenue → 1-1.5 m EUR (INR11-16 cr), offsetting HAT runoff.

- **Sample-to-answer system** — via OEM (not in-house dev); validation ongoing, "initial results good"; expect 2-3 lab installs from Q3 FY27 onward (already baked into 15-20% guidance).

- **TRUPCR Europe (UK):** INR20.67 cr, ~40% 4-yr CAGR; faces competition but managing.
- **Coris (Belgium, AMR rapid diagnostics):** ~INR50 cr annualised; AMR is growth/margin driver; ~23% of remaining (non-AMR: respiratory, Entero) under Chinese low-price pressure; HAT contract = EUR6 m total (2024, 4-yr), ~EUR3.45 m executed, ~EUR2.4 m remaining through FY28 (Congo-specific, Ebola risk to timing).

- M&A roll-up funded by ~INR230 cr treasury (see §9).

- Consolidated margin dragged to ~40% by Coris (~10% EBITDA) + TRUPCR (~15-20%).

capex: - Minimal — running ~50% capacity; capacity addition would cost only ~INR4-5 cr. No large organic capex; growth is asset-light + inorganic.
